item.title: listItems follows next_cursor
item.brief: Update listItems(transport) in inventory-client to follow the paginated GET /items contract: request the first page with no cursor, keep requesting while next_cursor is a non-null value, pass the cursor back unchanged, and resolve to all items in order. Treat an absent next_cursor as the last page. Add or update tests with a fake transport that returns multiple pages, covering ordering, the first request having no cursor, and the stop condition. Update the README to document the paginated behaviour. Keep `npm test` passing. Commit locally; do not push.

item.title: Cursor pagination for GET /items
item.brief: Add cursor pagination to GET /items in inventory-api, exactly as the shared contract specifies. Validate limit and cursor at the request boundary and return 400 with {"error": ...} for invalid values. Order items by id and make the cursor opaque to clients. Add unit tests covering: default limit, limit bounds (0, 1, 100, 101, non-integer), cursor round-trip across pages, last page next_cursor null, invalid cursor 400. Update the README to document the query parameters, the new response shape and the 400 errors. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Commit locally; do not push.

pr.body: Approach: keyset pagination on id. cursor is base64 of the last id on the previous page; decoding accepts only the exact canonical form, with the id bounded to 18 digits. limit accepts 1-3 digits (leading zeros allowed) and is range-checked. Non-string query values return 400. Key files: api.py (list_items, _parse_limit, _encode_cursor, _decode_cursor), test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 11 tests OK at 2c8e03b. Review: three whole-change reviewers failed 26506d2 on blocking cursor issues, fixed in 2c8e03b; a delta reviewer passed 2c8e03b. Assumptions and limits: the default of 20 changes the no-limit response (previously all items), which the contract requires; the owner must confirm. Cursors are not signed, so any well-formed canonical cursor is accepted. Follow-ups: get_item uses str.isdigit, which accepts superscript digits (pre-existing, not in this change).
pr.summary: GET /items returns one page: limit 1..100 (default 20) and next_cursor, ordered by id. before: all items, no paging. now: paged, opaque cursor, 400 on bad limit or cursor.

agt_01M8GNQ2CW2GP5DKCSBAS6KTSJ:1.description: _decode_cursor calls int(raw) outside its try block. A well-formed base64 cursor that decodes to more than 4300 digits makes int() raise ValueError, which propagates out of handle() instead of returning 400 invalid cursor. Verified with a 5000-digit cursor in a mktemp copy. The test suite has no oversized-cursor case, so this is not caught. at api.py:72

agt_01M8GNQ2CW2GP5DKCSBAS6KTSJ:2.description: README says a cursor 'not produced by this service' returns 400, but the code has no provenance check and accepts any well-formed base64 digit string. Verified: cursor 'MTA=' (id 10, never issued) returns 200. Cursor 'MT!!A==' also returns 200, because urlsafe_b64decode silently drops non-alphabet characters. Either sign or validate cursors, or correct the README and the 'only from a previous resp

agt_01M8GNQ2CW2GP5DKCSBAS6KTSJ:3.description: Non-string query values crash instead of returning 400. Verified: limit=5 raises TypeError in re.fullmatch, and cursor=5 raises AttributeError on .encode. The documented request shape is {str: str}, so this is a boundary-hardening gap, not a contract break. at api.py:67

agt_01M8GNQ2CW2GP5DKCSBAS6KTSJ:4.description: CLAUDE.md assertion density is not met. _parse_limit and _decode_cursor have zero assertions. The one assert in list_items (line 44) is decorative, since the slice already guarantees it. _encode_cursor's assert is meaningful. at api.py:49

agt_01M8GNQ2CW2GP5DKCSBAS6KTSJ:5.description: The cursor round-trip loop is while True with no iteration bound. If next_cursor ever stops advancing, the test hangs instead of failing. Add a bounded loop with a clear failure message. at test_api.py:46

agt_01M8GNQ7P5SR6722PXV858P2DP:2.description: Lenient base64 decoding accepts cursors the service never produced, contrary to README.md:17 (400 for a cursor not produced by this service).
